cohort: This study analyzed 4,902,675 live births registered in the Spanish Statistical Birth Bulletin between 2010 and 2021, including all live births with a registered type of delivery.
finding: The study found that maternal age >40 years, preterm births at 28-32 weeks, male newborn, and deliveries during the COVID-19 pandemic were risk factors for cesarean section, while weekend deliveries, non-Spanish maternal nationality, and larger municipality size were protective factors.
mod_finding: The primary outcome of the study was delivery type (mode of birth), and it identified various sociodemographic and birth-related factors associated with an increased or decreased likelihood of cesarean delivery.
cross-section timing: Data was collected from births registered between 2010 and 2021.
gest_age: Preterm births at 28-32 weeks were included as an exposure factor associated with CS.
